title: A Ceiling Is Not a Cable
concept: On October 21st the board of AIDEA, Alaska's state development authority, voted for a new wholly owned company, Northstar Fiber Development LLC, that can put up to $75 million into subsea and land fiber. Alaska reaches the Lower 48 on four undersea cables (three land in Oregon, one in Washington) and one land route, two of the cables from 1999 against a typical design life of about 25 years per AIDEA, and no cable connects Alaska directly to Asia. The resolution lists a link to the Pacific coast first, Asia third as explore and collaborate, requires capacity to land in Alaska, picks no project, partner or route, requires a finance plan and binding customer commitments before any binding commitment, and ends the authority on December 31st, 2028. Neither AIDEA document says AI, data center or compute, so the AI link is Alaska.Ai's own framing, and the economic studies the resolution cites are Nordic and European. Pip, a faced brass question token, travels in every shot. The film grants the guardrails and the documented need, narrows the claim to a starting gun and ends where it began.

palette: cream chart paper, graphite pencil and a cobalt sea cutaway with a brass question token and vermilion on the locks and clock
divergence_note: The last five films were an aubergine dusk depot (10-29), a green-black sonar abyss (10-28), a sage civic hall (10-26), a teal fog boardwalk (10-25) and a navy orbit (10-24). This film is daylight on cream chart paper with graphite pencil lines and a cobalt sea shown only as a cutaway. Its hero is a faced brass question token, its stage is a chart desk and a brass scale, and it has no night sky, no hall, no depot, no boardwalk and no orbit. The look is a map being drawn, the throughline is a graphite pencil line that never reaches its end, and the signature object is a labelled scale that walks to level one weight at a time.

treatment.winner: Explainer spine (a travelling question rides the cables, the Two-Pan Scale test, two locks loop, Asia wall loop)
treatment.judge_reasoning: All four lenses converged on one spine. The Explainer's pitch was chosen for its three scale reveals, its Test staged as a scale with a pan that sinks and re-levels (so the fair case against the film is drawn at full strength), and its two loops 18s apart. Grafts: the Dramatist's cul-de-sac sign gag and binder-that-does-not-fit gag (Nordic coastline), the Comedian's 1999 birthday-hat gag and magnifier that finds AI only inside AIDEA, the Enthusiast's postcards-of-interest sliding off the keyhole. Rejected: a net-new SPOOL hero (cost, and a second faced object competes with the traveller), the sea otter runner, the BEAD lower third (c19/c20 cut as last-mile and blurring Northstar's ceiling).
treatment.hero: Pip, a faced brass question token (lib/fiber.tsx), a faced cousin of the shelf QuestionToken drawn fresh
treatment.throughline: Pip's engraving: ? / VIA LOWER 48 / UP TO $75M / WHO SIGNS? / ?
treatment.signature_shot: Shot 10 (88.06 to 98.42 s) as one continuous move: the labelled scale rolls in, the binder sinks THE DOUBTS pan, then one weight per beat (the gauge plate at 'ceiling', the locks and the landing stamp at 'rule', the 1999 tag at 'cables') walk the needle to level with Pip riding it. Camera: a short truckAcross that resolves into a lock at zoom 1.0 from the first weight to the end of the shot.
treatment.loops: Asia wall planted 14s, paid by the Asia third line; the date planted in the ceiling line, paid by the 2028 clock

angle.thesis: A ceiling is not a cable. Every Alaskan connection to the wider world, a chatbot question included, leaves on four aging undersea cables that land in Oregon and Washington, and AIDEA's new Northstar Fiber Development is a well-guarded option to add a door, whose test is whether bound customers sign before December 31st, 2028.
supporting_facts: c5/c6/c7/c8 four subsea cables plus one land route, three land in Oregon and one in Washington, two from 1999 against a typical 25 year design life per AIDEA
c9/c10/c12 AIDEA's own digital cul-de-sac line, no cable direct to Asia, Asia third and only explore and collaborate
c14/c15/c16 no project, partner or route, binding customer commitments required, authority ends December 31st, 2028
angle.counterpoint_honored: Conditions, a ceiling and a landing rule are how careful public money should look, and the need is documented (c3, c13, c8). The film grants all of it, then narrows the claim: the economics AIDEA cites are Nordic and European (c18), and neither document says AI (c17), so the AI link is Alaska.Ai's own framing.
angle.falsifiable: False if the authority reaches December 31st, 2028 with no finance plan and no binding customer commitment ever being needed, or if any Alaska cable reached Asia directly or the four landed anywhere but the Pacific Northwest.
runner_ups: Enthusiast: a door built before choosing where it leads (loses: cheerleading with no route)
Dramatist: a permission slip, not a cable (loses: right facts, sour frame)
angle.cross_challenge: Three analysts each red-teamed their own thesis against c14, c15 and c18, and the synthesis adopts the stricter falsifier. No separate cross-challenge round ran.
